analysis.title: Greenbrier Cos. (GBX): 4Q26 (Aug) EPS Miss; FY27 EPS Guide Below Consensus; Remain Sell-Rated
key_insights: GBX (Sell) reported fiscal 4Q26 core adjusted EPS of $0.39 versus $0.80 FactSet consensus and $0.73 GSe. Revenue of $591M was about 2% below consensus of $605M.
Consolidated EBIT of about $31M was roughly 29% below consensus of $43M. The consolidated margin was 5.2% versus 7.2% consensus.
FY27 EPS guidance was initiated at $2.75-$3.75. The $3.25 midpoint is about 11% below the $3.65 consensus coming into the print.

GS cut its FY27 EPS estimate from $3.70 to $3.10, below the guidance midpoint, citing conservatism on railcar deliveries and manufacturing margin trajectory. The FY28 estimate went from $4.80 to $4.40.

Manufacturing railcar deliveries fell 30% YoY versus a 28% GS forecast, after declines of 39% in fiscal 3Q and 32% in 2Q. Manufacturing gross margin was 9.2% versus 9.5% GSe, down from about 14% a year ago.

Railcar manufacturing backlog was 14,000 units, up slightly from 13,800 last quarter but down from 15,200 in fiscal 2Q and 16,600 a year ago. Backlog improved sequentially for the first time since 2024, with book-to-bill still slightly below 1x.

Leasing revenue was about $52M versus about $55M consensus. Leasing gross profit was $30M versus $34M consensus, a margin of about 58% versus 62% consensus. Management attributed this to maintenance timing and expects normal margins ahead.

The stock is down 19% YTD through the 10/26 close. GS says this partly reflects uncertainty around antidumping and countervailing duty (AD/CVD) petitions filed by a competitor, which argue that producing tank cars in Mexico gives GBX and Trinity a cost advantage over domestic producers such as UTLX.

The AD/CVD investigations could run into 2027, with a couple of months for preliminary determinations and 200+ days for final determinations. GS says they could over time lead to higher railcar prices and manufacturing margin compression from higher input costs, with possibly higher maintenance margins if shippers lean on existing fleets.
CEO Lorie Tekorius will step down effective Jan 6, 2027. EVP and Americas President Brian Comstock, with nearly three decades at Greenbrier, is the named successor.

GS keeps its Sell rating because it sees weaker manufacturing as more impactful to near-term financials than the solid backdrop for railcar leasing. It sees estimate revisions biased to the downside for GBX and to the upside for Buy-rated GATX.

The 12-month price target is $36 (from $38), at 10.5x base, 9.5x bear and 13.0x bull P/E multiples on Q5-Q8 EPS of $4.40, $2.78 and $6.06. The weightings are 50%/50%/0% base/bear/bull. Downside to the $38.30 price is 6.0%.
FY27 guidance also includes revenue of $2.8B-$3.2B, aggregate gross margin of about 14-15% and operating margin of 7.0%-7.5%. It assumes industry deliveries of 26,000-28,000 units and tax of 26-29%.

market_movers.rationale: Fiscal 4Q26 EPS missed consensus by about half and FY27 guidance came in below the Street. GS lowered its target from $38 to $36 and its FY27 EPS estimate from $3.70 to $3.10.

GS sees estimate revisions biased to the upside for GATX. It is working through synergies from the book-value acquisition of Wells Fargo's railcar fleet, with ongoing strength in secondary market gains on sale.

sector_views.rationale: Muted railcar deliveries and ordering weigh on manufacturing earnings in the near term. Pure-play leasing has a solid backdrop, helped by higher railcar prices.

earnings_insights: GBX fiscal 4Q26 (Aug) adjusted diluted EPS was $0.39 reported versus $0.80 FactSet consensus and $0.73 GSe.
GBX 4Q26 revenue was $591M reported versus $605M consensus and $607M GSe. Gross profit was $80M versus $90M GSe, and operating profit was $31.0M versus $43M consensus and $43.9M GSe.

GBX 4Q26 manufacturing revenue was $539M, in line with consensus. Manufacturing gross profit was $50M versus $57M consensus, and gross margin was 9.2% versus 10.6% consensus. Deliveries were 3,200 versus 3,312 GSe.

GBX 4Q26 leasing revenue was $52M versus $55M consensus. Leasing gross profit was $30M versus $34M consensus, and gross margin was 57.6% versus 61.7% consensus. Fleet utilization was 98.0% versus 98.5% GSe.

Below the EBIT line, interest and FX of $19.3M was higher than GSe $15.8M. Unconsolidated affiliate income of $7.1M was above the $4.0M GS estimate. Gains on lease portfolio sales were $1.7M versus $4.5M GSe.
FY27 EPS guidance range is $2.75-$3.75, versus FactSet consensus of $3.65 before the print and GS's prior $3.70 estimate. GS now estimates $3.10 (one passage in the report says $3.20).

GS estimates FY27 EPS of $3.10 (from $3.70) and FY28 EPS of $4.40 (from $4.80). Quarterly EPS estimates are $0.71 for 11/26E, $0.58 for 2/27E and $0.90 for 5/27E. GS FY27E revenue is $2,815.8M (from $2,434.4M) and EBITDA is $348.8M.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS says recent positive ISM-manufacturing readings could prove a green shoot for GBX's manufacturing business. It still expects railcar ordering to stay tempered.
This is company guidance, and GS describes industry deliveries in 2027 as relatively muted.

risk_factors: Upside risks to the Sell rating: faster recovery in manufacturing deliveries from a freight market recovery or higher industry railcar needs.
Upside risks to the Sell rating: better manufacturing margins from structural and variable cost takeout, or accelerated leasing gains that offset manufacturing weakness.
The valuation multiple could move closer to peers faster than expected, from faster margin catch-up or leasing build-out, or an industry re-rating toward long-term averages.

Near-term railcar ordering could stay tempered by uncertain railroad and industrial capex under an evolving tariff situation, continued rail network efficiency (including a possible UNP/NSC merger), a more disciplined railcar builder environment, and uncertain underlying demand.
AD/CVD investigations may lead to noise and uncertainty into 2027. A CEO transition takes effect Jan 6, 2027.
geopolitical: Antidumping and countervailing duty petitions were filed by a competitor on tank cars produced in Mexico versus the US, naming GBX and Trinity. The evolving tariff situation adds uncertainty to railroad and industrial capex plans.

tension_points.bull_case: Several consecutive quarters of solidly positive rail carload growth could spur railcar ordering. Backlog improved sequentially for the first time since 2024, and structural savings should lift earnings on recovery.
tension_points.bear_case: Deliveries are down 30% YoY, manufacturing margin is 9.2%, and FY27 guidance is below consensus. There is a limited catalyst path to meaningful delivery uplift, and AD/CVD adds uncertainty.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Faster-than-anticipated recovery in manufacturing deliveries, better manufacturing margins from cost takeout, or accelerated leasing gains that offset manufacturing weakness would challenge the Sell rating.

theme_stances.key_argument: Weaker manufacturing deliveries and margins make the near-term set-up tougher for GBX, with estimate revisions biased to the downside.
theme_stances.evidence: bias around estimate revisions to the downside

theme_stances.key_argument: Higher railcar prices and secondary market gains on sale support the pure-play leasing backdrop, and GATX estimate revisions are biased upward.
theme_stances.evidence: still-solid fundamental backdrop for pure-play railcar leasing
